svg.text: A Rank of each peak in the two replicates
rank in replicate 1 (1 = strongest)
rank in replicate 2
simulated; colour = truth, which IDR has to estimate
strong peaks:
similar ranks in both
(near the diagonal)
weak peaks / noise:
ranks unrelated
(a scattered cloud)
B What IDR does
Call peaks leniently in each replicate
(e.g. MACS3 -p 0.01, keep the top 300 000).
Match peaks between replicates by overlap;
rank each by its score (p-value or signal).
Fit a mixture: a reproducible component
(correlated ranks) + an irreproducible one.
IDR of a peak = the chance that it belongs
to the irreproducible part, given its ranks.
Keep peaks with IDR ≤ 0.05: a cutoff on
agreement, not on one replicate's p-value.
Naive overlap only asks "is it in both?", and its answer
changes with the threshold you happened to pick.
